response.title: what are the main differences between the Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + 220W solar panel, the Goal Zero Yeti 1500X and the Zendure SuperBase V
response.answer:
The Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + 220W solar panel, Goal Zero Yeti 1500X, and Zendure SuperBase V are all portable power stations, but they're designed for somewhat different needs.

The biggest differences are battery capacity, power output, charging speed, portability, and expandability.

In short:

Jackery 1000 v2: Best for portability, camping, and relatively simple backup power.

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus: Best balance of fast charging, modern features, and everyday versatility.

Goal Zero Yeti 1500X: Larger battery than the first two, but an older and heavier design.

Zendure SuperBase V: Designed for serious home backup, with much larger capacity and expansion options.

The **Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2**, **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + 220W solar panel**, **Goal Zero Yeti 1500X**, and **Zendure SuperBase V** are all portable power stations, but they're designed for somewhat different needs.

The biggest differences are **battery capacity, power output, charging speed, portability, and expandability**.

In short:

- **Jackery 1000 v2:** Best for portability, camping, and relatively simple backup power.
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus:** Best balance of fast charging, modern features, and everyday versatility.
- **Goal Zero Yeti 1500X:** Larger battery than the first two, but an older and heavier design.
- **Zendure SuperBase V:** Designed for serious home backup, with much larger capacity and expansion options.

## 1. Side-by-side specifications

These are the published US specifications for the power stations, excluding the weight of solar panels.

| Feature | Jackery 1000 v2 | EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus | Goal Zero Yeti 1500X | Zendure SuperBase V |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Battery capacity | 1,070 Wh | 1,024 Wh | 1,516 Wh | 4,608–6,438 Wh |
| Continuous AC output | 1,500 W | 1,800 W | 2,000 W | ~3,800 W |
| Battery chemistry | LiFePO4 | LiFePO4 | Lithium NMC | LiFePO4 / semi-solid-state |
| Weight | 23.8 lb | 27.6 lb | 45.6 lb | 121–130 lb |
| Max solar input | 400 W | 1,000 W | 600 W | Up to 3,000 W |
| AC outlets | 3 | 6 | 2 | Multiple |
| Battery expansion | No | Yes | Yes, with accessories | Yes, extensive |
| Primary advantage | Lightweight | Versatility | Larger standalone battery | Home backup |

<caption>Zendure figures depend on whether you choose the V4600 or V6400. Manufacturer specifications: <Cite refs={["turn328260search1","turn177837search1","turn177837search2","turn328260search5"]}/></caption>

## 2. Battery capacity: How long can they run appliances?

This is arguably the most important distinction.

  <text weight="medium" size="sm">Battery capacity comparison</text>
  {#each [{n:"Jackery 1000 v2",v:1070},{n:"EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus",v:1024},{n:"Goal Zero Yeti 1500X",v:1516},{n:"Zendure V4600",v:4608},{n:"Zendure V6400",v:6438}] as p}

      </box>
    </box>
  {/each}
</box>

Here is an estimated runtime comparison for common devices, assuming approximately 85% usable battery energy through the AC inverter.

| Appliance | Jackery | EcoFlow | Goal Zero | Zendure V4600 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50W fan | 18 hr | 17 hr | 26 hr | 78 hr |
| 100W TV | 9 hr | 9 hr | 13 hr | 39 hr |
| 500W appliance | 1.8 hr | 1.7 hr | 2.6 hr | 7.8 hr |

These are theoretical estimates for continuous loads. Actual runtime varies with inverter losses, standby consumption, temperature, and appliance cycling. Refrigerators, for example, do not normally run continuously.

  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>

  </grid-item>

  </grid-item>

The **EcoFlow has the strongest solar charging flexibility among the three smaller units**. Its 1,000W solar input ceiling is more than double the Jackery's.

One important distinction: a 220W panel doesn't continuously deliver 220W. Cloud cover, sunlight angle, heat, and shading all affect charging. <Cite refs={["turn328260search0","turn177837search1","turn177837search12","turn177837search3"]}/>

## 4. Battery lifespan and durability

The Jackery and EcoFlow use modern lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) batteries, while the older Yeti 1500X uses NMC cells.

| Model | Manufacturer-rated cycle life |
|---|---|
| Jackery 1000 v2 | 4,000 cycles to 70% capacity |
| EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus | 4,000 cycles to 80% capacity |
| Goal Zero Yeti 1500X | 500 cycles to 80% capacity |
| Zendure V4600 | 6,000 cycles to 60% capacity |
| Zendure V6400 | 3,000 cycles to 60% capacity |

These ratings use different remaining-capacity thresholds, so they're not perfectly comparable. Still, the Yeti 1500X has a significant disadvantage for frequent daily cycling. <Cite refs={["turn328260search1","turn177837search1","turn177837search0","turn328260search5"]}/>

text:
The Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + 220W solar panel, Goal Zero Yeti 1500X, and Zendure SuperBase V are all portable power stations, but they're designed for somewhat different needs.

The biggest differences are battery capacity, power output, charging speed, portability, and expandability.

In short:

Jackery 1000 v2: Best for portability, camping, and relatively simple backup power.

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus: Best balance of fast charging, modern features, and everyday versatility.

Goal Zero Yeti 1500X: Larger battery than the first two, but an older and heavier design.

Zendure SuperBase V: Designed for serious home backup, with much larger capacity and expansion options.

These are theoretical estimates for continuous loads. Actual runtime varies with inverter losses, standby consumption, temperature, and appliance cycling. Refrigerators, for example, do not normally run continuously.

3. Solar charging differences
Shop

Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2

Maximum solar input is 400W. A typical 200W bundle is suitable for camping but relatively slow for solar-only recharging.

Shop

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus

Up to 1,000W solar input across two ports. The included 220W bifacial panel is a useful start, and you can add more compatible panels.

Shop

Goal Zero Yeti 1500X

Up to 600W solar input. Its larger battery needs more sunlight to recharge using the same-sized panel.

Shop

Zendure SuperBase V

Supports substantially larger solar arrays, making it more appropriate for extended backup or off-grid installations.

The EcoFlow has the strongest solar charging flexibility among the three smaller units. Its 1,000W solar input ceiling is more than double the Jackery's.

One important distinction: a 220W panel doesn't continuously deliver 220W. Cloud cover, sunlight angle, heat, and shading all affect charging.

4. Battery lifespan and durability

The Jackery and EcoFlow use modern lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) batteries, while the older Yeti 1500X uses NMC cells.

These ratings use different remaining-capacity thresholds, so they're not perfectly comparable. Still, the Yeti 1500X has a significant disadvantage for frequent daily cycling.

5. Which one should you buy?

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus

Best overall
My top choice for most people. It has a powerful inverter, fast charging, expandable storage, six AC outlets, and a UPS transfer time under 10ms. The 220W solar bundle makes it particularly versatile.

Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2

Best for camping, road trips, and portability. It weighs almost 4 lb less than the EcoFlow, with slightly more battery capacity. Choose it if portability matters more than expandability.

Goal Zero Yeti 1500X

Best if you specifically need around 1.5kWh of capacity and find it at a substantial discount. Its older battery chemistry, weight, and charging system make it less attractive than newer alternatives at similar prices.

Zendure SuperBase V

Best for extended power outages and larger home backup systems. Its capacity and expandability are in a completely different class, but it's too heavy and expensive for typical camping use.

My recommendation: Unless you need multi-day home backup, I'd narrow the choice to the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus and Jackery 1000 v2. EcoFlow wins on functionality; Jackery wins on portability.

One question that would help me make a more specific recommendation: Are you primarily buying this for home power outages, camping/RV use, or running particular appliances? That can change which model offers the best value.
